Hi Elena — thanks for your patience. We completed our internal analysis and here's the outcome:

Summary:
- Event window observed: 20:32–20:47 ET on 2026-12-04.
- Root cause: hybrid — initial CDN edge routing change declared by the provider (20:29–20:34 ET) likely introduced request routing variation, but our tracing shows that after 20:34 the majority (~62%) of degraded traces had elevated service_time within Redwood's runtime (cache warmup + suboptimal kernel path triggered under the traffic shape).

How we calculated uptime and credit:
- Monthly uptime is computed as (total minutes in month - minutes of qualifying degradation) / total minutes in month. For concentrated partial degradations we apply time-weighted apportionment to compute the availability impact on the monthly SLA.
- Because >50% of the impact during the window maps to Redwood's runtime, the event is not fully excluded as a third-party outage.
- Given the concentrated impact during a customer-critical period, and per precedent, Redwood will issue a one-time 7% service credit on your Dec invoice. This is a goodwill and operational responsibility recognition, not an admission of systemic SLA failure.

Next steps:
- Credit: one-time 7% service credit (applied to Dec invoice).
- Postmortem: we will publish a short postmortem link and a brief mitigation plan (edge routing hardening + cache-warmup improvements) in 48 hours: https://redwood.example.com/postmortem/INC-20261204-GLM
- If you'd like escalated technical detail, Marcus can set up a 30-minute review with your SREs.

Attachments included: incident-log-20261204.csv, trace-summary-20261204.txt, postmortem-draft-20261206.md

Apologies again for the impact during a critical window. We appreciate the detailed signal you provided — that materially improved our ability to apportion responsibility.
